prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a horizontal clothing rack in the immediate foreground across all five frames, within arm's reach of the camera wearer at roughly 0.4 to 1.0 metres, with architectural walls, pillars, and glass storefronts receding from about 1.5 to over 4 metres in the background. In frames 1 and 4, two upright mannequins stand immediately behind the right end of the rack at roughly 1.2 to 1.8 metres (about 0.4 metres apart from each other), while in frames 3 and 5 a hooded person stands behind the left side of the rack at roughly 1.5 to 2.0 metres, facing away or sideways rather than looking toward the camera wearer, with their lower body occluded by the hanging garments and the rack itself cropped at the bottom of the frame. Across the five frames, the camera wearer pans and tilts left in frames 2 and 3 before turning right and approaching closer to the clothing rack in frames 4 and 5, where the rack bar and shirts become brightest at under 0.6 metres. Compared to the motion-blurred RGB strip, the depth map clearly separates the near horizontal rack bar and individual hanger hooks from the background clutter, as well as the silhouettes of the person's head in frames 3 and 5 and the mannequins in frame 4. However, the depth map is unreliable on the glass storefront window, where bright reflections and the circular red window decal are misestimated as dark, distant voids or flat surfaces rather than the true plane of the glass.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map fails to capture most of the scene layout, missing the walls, storefront window, and the clothing rack entirely in frames 2 and 3 while only outputting isolated masks in frames 1, 4, and 5. In frame 1, it detects only the upper half of the red circular graphic on the window (around 2 to 3 metres away to the left behind the rack) and misclassifies it as an 'umbrella', occluded at the bottom by the unsegmented clothing rack in front of it. In frame 4, it misclassifies the hanging garments at the bottom of the frame (within arm's reach at 0.5 to 0.8 metres) as a 'person' while failing to segment the actual mannequins standing just above and behind them at 1.2 to 1.5 metres. In frame 5, it segments the hooded head of the person standing about 1.5 metres away on the left behind the rack (facing away from the camera wearer with their torso occluded by the clothes), but assigns a duplicate 'person' label and merges the foreground clothing rack (0.4 to 0.8 metres away) and part of the right-hand window decal into a single brown person/object mask. While the segmentation map helps isolate the small, dark-hooded head in the upper-left of frame 5 against the window frame, it is largely unreliable due to severe false positives on the hanging clothes and window decal and complete false negatives across the middle frames.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely blank across frames 1, 2, 3, and 5, detecting a single yellow body skeleton only in the lower-middle region of frame 4 and no magenta hand skeletons in any frame. In frame 4, this detected skeleton is falsely placed on the shoulders and sleeves of the garments hanging on the foreground rack within arm's reach (roughly 0.5 to 0.7 metres in front of and below the camera wearer's eye level), hallucinating a cluster of facial keypoints near the hanger hooks and a shoulder-arm triangle extending to the bottom edge of the frame as if a person were facing the camera wearer. The actual hooded person standing about 1.5 to 2.0 metres away behind the left side of the rack in frames 3 and 5—who faces away and sideways from the camera wearer with their body below the neck occluded by the hanging clothes—is completely missed as the camera pans left and right across the sequence. The two upright mannequins standing behind the right side of the rack at 1.2 to 1.8 metres in frames 1 and 4 are also unrepresented in the pose map. Consequently, the pose map adds no reliable spatial information beyond what is in the RGB strip and is highly unreliable here due to severe occlusion of the real person by the foreground rack and a false-positive skeleton triggered by clothing on hangers.
